findings_to_judge.finding: The two inputs nobody watching MAMA is tracking are benign in exactly this quarter: CME 40-lb block cheddar closed $1.5050/lb on 2026-07-08, near the bottom of its own 2022-2026 $1.30-$2.40 range, and retail boneless chicken breast averaged $4.15/lb in July 2026, down 1.2% year over year with breast-meat supply called balanced-to-heavy through end-2026 - so the Q1 gross-margin shortfall the market de-rated the stock for, which the CFO quantified on the June 8 call as ~$0.5-1.0m of one-time launch labour/material inefficiency plus ~$0.5m reclassified from marketing to trade, was not a commodity problem and does not have a commodity reason to repeat.

Fiscal Q2 (May 1 - Jul 31 2026) is the first full quarter of revenue from the 2,000 Walmart and 750 Target deli doors, which management said on 2026-06-08 'did not launch till the middle to end of April - so we had all the costs... The cost is all in Q1. But really, very little of the revenue was in Q1' - i.e. the costs and the revenue were split across the quarter boundary in the company's favour, and the market has sold the stock 15.8% in 20 sessions into that split with no company news since the 2026-08-20 earnings-date notice.

MAMA raised $94m net at $18.00/share on 2026-06-30 explicitly to fund 'the acquisition of businesses or other assets', has filed no 8-K item 1.01/2.01 in the two months since, and has form for announcing deals into this exact calendar slot: on 2026's equivalent week last year it filed the Crown I asset purchase plus a $20m private placement (8-K dated 2025-09-02, event 2025-08-28) six days before the Q2 print and the stock moved +14.4% that day.

The one customer-side datapoint published after MAMA last spoke cuts the other way: Albertsons on 2026-07-23 cut its FY2026 identical-sales outlook from 0.0%-1.0% to (1.5)%-(0.5)% and cut EBITDA guidance, reporting identical sales -0.8% for the 16 weeks ended 2026-06-20 and citing 'core grocery... increasing pressure from softer industry unit trends and a more cautious consumer' - a window that sits inside MAMA's May-July fiscal Q2, on a company whose banners are perimeter-deli customers.
